title: Clayface Sets December 8 Digital Release as Global Box Office Tops $126 Million
excerpt:
DC's horror-focused Clayface will arrive on digital platforms on December 8, 2026.
Its worldwide box office has passed $126 million, while an HBO Max date remains unconfirmed.
body_md:
DC's horror-oriented Clayface is moving into its home-viewing window relatively quickly. The film is scheduled for digital release on December 8, 2026, roughly 45 days after its theatrical debut. That announcement establishes a date for digital availability, not a confirmed subscription-streaming premiere. No official HBO Max launch date was provided in the report.

The story follows Matt Hagen, an actor whose face is disfigured by members of the local mafia. Seeking a way to restore his appearance, he agrees to an experimental procedure. Its consequences transform him into Clayface and send him on a path of revenge. Rather than relying on the conventional spectacle of a major superhero crossover, the film uses horror and physical transformation to explore a familiar Batman adversary from a different perspective.

The digital announcement arrives while the movie is still earning money theatrically. Its worldwide total has passed $126 million, with the report citing approximately $126.2 million. That places it close to the reported $126.5 million worldwide finish of Supergirl. The article anticipates Clayface overtaking that figure, but the figures it supplies do not yet establish that the crossover has occurred.

The comparison also illustrates how differently the two films were financed. Supergirl is described as having a production budget of approximately $170 million. For Clayface, however, the source is internally inconsistent: its headline refers to a $30 million movie, while the article body says the budget was $40 million. Neither figure should be treated as definitively verified from this report alone. Under either estimate, the horror film was made at a much smaller scale than a typical effects-heavy superhero blockbuster.

That lower production cost is central to the commercial discussion surrounding James Gunn's approach to the project. A worldwide gross exceeding $126 million is encouraging relative to the reported production spend, but box office revenue cannot be equated directly with profit. Theaters retain part of ticket sales, and marketing and distribution costs must also be considered before making a definitive profitability claim.

The article speculates that an HBO Max arrival could follow the digital window and that Blu-ray and 4K editions might come later, potentially in January. Those are projections rather than announced dates. For now, December 8 is the concrete home-release milestone. The broader question is whether a relatively contained, genre-specific comic-book adaptation can encourage more variety in DC's film slate, even as the company's future production strategy remains uncertain.
